paper_metadata.title: Quantum Monte Carlo Simulations for predicting electron-positron pair production via the linear Breit-Wheeler process

experiments.description: Ideal-simulator quantum Monte Carlo experiment for linear Breit-Wheeler pair production using three alternative state-preparation methods (Qiskit native initialization, variational initialization, and Fourier Series Loader) while varying the monoenergetic photon energy.

algorithm.variant: Iterative Quantum Amplitude Estimation (IQAE) with polynomially embedded Breit-Wheeler probability
algorithm.ansatz: Variational CNOT-Ry ring ansatz for state preparation; Fourier-series-based state loading; Qiskit native initialization
algorithm.convergence_criteria: Iterative amplitude estimation until target accuracy/confidence interval is satisfied

problem_formulation.encoding_details: Photon energy distribution is discretized over a work register; probabilities are embedded into an ancilla via controlled rotations; the Breit-Wheeler probability is approximated by a second-degree polynomial and loaded into ancilla rotations.
problem_formulation.objective_function: Estimate the expected number of electron-positron pairs N_pairs = N_int * E[p(X)] for head-on gamma-gamma collisions via the linear Breit-Wheeler probability.
problem_formulation.constraints_handling: Probability function is rescaled to [0,1] before ancilla rotation; no explicit constraint optimization.

problem_instance.description: Head-on collision of two gamma-photon beams; one monoenergetic beam and one Gaussian-like energy distribution; pair production via linear Breit-Wheeler.
data_preprocessing_details: Approximate Breit-Wheeler cross-section with a second-degree polynomial
Discretize energy distribution on a qubit register
problem_instance.evaluation_methodology: Compare quantum-simulated pair counts against theoretical predictions across varying monoenergetic beam energies.

classical_postprocessing: Convert measured amplitude to expected pair probability
Multiply by number of interacting particles to obtain expected number of pairs

speedup_claims.conditions: using amplitude estimation / IQAE in the idealized setting
speedup_claims.caveats: The paper notes that the theoretical quadratic speedup is limited in practice by polynomial approximation and state-preparation approximations.

complexity_analysis.quantum_complexity: Theoretically quadratic speedup over classical Monte Carlo via amplitude estimation; exact asymptotic cost not specified
complexity_analysis.classical_complexity: Monte Carlo sampling scales as O(1/epsilon^2) for accuracy epsilon

experiments.description: Trapped-ion quantum hardware experiment running the linear Breit-Wheeler quantum Monte Carlo algorithm on IonQ Forte Enterprise, comparing Fourier Series Loader and variational state preparation across monoenergetic beam energies.

algorithm.variant: Iterative Quantum Amplitude Estimation (IQAE) on hardware
algorithm.ansatz: Variational CNOT-Ry ring ansatz; Fourier-series loading
algorithm.convergence_criteria: Iterative amplitude estimation until target accuracy/confidence interval is satisfied

problem_formulation.encoding_details: Three-qubit work register initialized with a parametric circuit and Fourier series; polynomial Breit-Wheeler probability embedded into ancilla rotations.
problem_formulation.objective_function: Estimate expected number of electron-positron pairs from head-on gamma-gamma collisions on hardware.
problem_formulation.constraints_handling: Probability rescaling to [0,1] and ancilla-controlled rotations.

problem_instance.evaluation_methodology: Compare QPU results against ideal simulations and theoretical predictions; report mean accuracy around 87% relative to theory.
